product_from_film: Harbor builds clinical study databases from protocols, extracts source data and helps monitors compare fields with source documents.
explains_well: The film connects sponsor setup, site data entry and monitoring, using the same study and side-by-side source evidence.
unclear: A potential issue and confidence score are shown, but the film does not show a reviewer correcting or approving the extracted value.
scenario: A sponsor uploads a protocol and customizes rules, a coordinator uploads visit documents, and a monitor checks extracted values against source pages.
product_clear_basis: The extraction/organization captions and side-by-side source document and demographic fields are visible by 16–17s; the EDC category is named at 25s.

sound.detail: The draft gives a coherent explanatory script for protocol setup, field rules, coordinator upload and monitor review. Opening wording, names and compliance terms have errors; visible captions support the broad story and exact displayed labels. No validated listening, voice delivery, music, effects or sync assessment.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V11; script and visible captions largely align in topic, not verified acoustic timing.

categories.finding: Administrative problem → product overview → sponsor setup → coordinator entry → monitor review → human-work benefit → URL.
Cropped articles claim slower and costlier trials, then a chart reinforces the trend; the product arrives later.
Clinical research teams are clear by the overview; sponsors, site coordinators and monitors each receive a task.
UI crops enlarge uploads, field properties and source highlights; photographic states show strain then clinical activity. Exact blur transitions are unresolved in sampled views.
Role changes return to human scenes before another UI sequence, helping organize the three workflows.
Bright clinical rooms and clean white UI contrast with crowded paper stacks and darker desk scenes. Purple and yellow mark extracted data.
Persistent captions explain the workflow. Enlarged rule names and source highlights improve readability, while longer panels remain dense.
The ASR and visible captions explain the three roles; draft errors are not used as exact quotations. Audible delivery remains unchecked.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Clinical and office scenes alternate with document and platform views. Their production method, source and representativeness are not established.
Source duration 120.02 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Captions, file upload and source-to-field highlights preserve the main explanation silently. Actual accuracy and time gains are not visually demonstrated.
Large cursors and close crops guide attention to the current control. The source checkbox and corresponding field provide a clear comparison target.
The two-minute film has distinct role sections, but the closing human-benefit passage is long relative to the missing review-resolution step.
Paper/computer burden is answered by automation and source-linked review, then scenes of staff with people. Measured trial acceleration is not shown.
Strained desk workers become calm and socially engaged, framing relief and care; audience response is unmeasured.
The Mobile ECG study, demographic forms and repeated source fields connect setup, entry and monitoring across roles.

The 80% time figure, two-hours-to-ten-minutes saving, regulatory compliance and better retention/faster trials are film claims. Displayed extraction and confidence scores do not verify accuracy or compliance.
Protocol-generated forms, clinical validation rules and linked source checkboxes make the platform specific.
Complete the monitor’s decision before the human-benefit close.
categories.experiment: Show a low-confidence field, the source check, a correction or approval and the saved audit entry.

categories.finding: For Tin, make generated claims traceable to their inputs.
categories.experiment: Show a campaign claim beside its source, let a reviewer correct it and display the accepted revision.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Give each role a concrete task and connect extracted fields to their source.
try: Show a low-confidence field being checked, corrected or approved and saved.
For Tin, link a campaign claim to its source and show the reviewer’s accepted revision.
lessons.avoid: Ending a review demonstration at the confidence score without the human decision.
lessons.open: Extraction accuracy, time savings, compliance, trial outcomes, asset origins and audio remain unverified.

comparison.story: Problem → sponsor setup → site entry → monitoring → human benefit.
comparison.motion: UI crops, cursors and colored source highlights among role scenes.
comparison.sound: Coherent ASR with errors; visible captions support story; no listening.
comparison.texture: White clinical UI, paper burden and bright human scenes.
comparison.lesson: Source-linked fields explain trust better when the review decision is also shown.

scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
